basis: Bone fragility, retinal/optic degeneration, seizures and severe developmental disability define the syndrome.
Inherited iron overload; hepatic injury with elevated transaminases in 5/7. Cardiac and joint damage are occasional; pigmentation alone does not establish skin injury.
Glycosylation disorder; developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage; MAGT1 alone does not establish immunodeficiency.
Immune-mediated fascial inflammation with characteristic cutaneous/subcutaneous induration and fibrosis. Reactive eosinophilia does not establish a blood disorder.
The umbrella is explicitly classified under both hereditary neurological disease and eye disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
Congenital muscular dystrophy; cognitive dysfunction in 80-99% and cardiac conduction disease in 30-79%. Respiratory distress reflects muscle weakness; cataracts are occasional.
Bilateral loss of labyrinthine reactivity is dysfunction of the inner-ear vestibular organs.
Folate transport defect with immunodeficiency and megaloblastic anemia; developmental/myelination defects in 75-100%. Oral ulcers (4/4) and skin ulcers (2/4) omitted at cap.
Clear-cell morphologic variant of carcinoma arising from hepatocytes.
Pulmonary arterial vascular disease with right ventricular failure in 3/5; both are cardiovascular. No direct lung parenchymal disease is established.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable sites; no organ within the remaining axes is consistently affected across the group.
Congenital duplication of central finger skeletal structures.
Psychiatric dissociative disorder; the definition excludes memory loss caused by a medical condition.
The definition identifies skeletal fusion, conductive deafness from stapes ankylosis, and ocular abnormalities including hyperopia and strabismus as characteristic features.
Benign pancreatic neoplasm classified under digestive-system disease; no endocrine origin or hormonal disorder is specified.
The supplied concept identifies cataract and skeletal anomalies; no definition or phenotype evidence supports additional axes.
Malignancy involving the bones of the limbs.
Magnesium deficiency is a nutritional electrolyte disorder. Cramps, paresthesias and confusion do not establish common direct structural organ damage.
Defined neurodevelopmental disorder; hearing impairment in 2/6 (~33%). Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Severe Zellweger metabolic/neurologic disease; hepatic dysfunction and ocular disease commonly affect >30%. Skeletal stippling and hearing loss omitted at cap.
BEST1-associated retinal degeneration with rod-cone dysfunction and progressive visual loss.
Monogenic diabetes umbrella. Nephropathy and retinopathy are separately coded complications; renal and exocrine pancreatic abnormalities occur in uncommon subtypes.
Craniofacial duplication with visual abnormalities; anencephaly and cardiac septal defects each 80-99%. Palatal, nasal and pinna anomalies omitted at cap.
Congenital cleft involving the laryngeal/tracheal and esophageal interface, producing abnormal airway-digestive communication.
Cranial/peripheral neuropathy and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define it; structural talipes occurs in 80-99%. Ophthalmoplegia reflects cranial nerve dysfunction.
